closed_reason: Fixed on feat-FEAT-103-external-provider-token-capture. Options (a) + (b) of the suggested fix, with (c) as an opt-in: (b) ExternalAuth.ensure_fresh_login_grant runs the captured grant through the same IDENTITY_REFRESH_LEEWAY check get_live_provider_token uses and refreshes before the grant reaches the provider userinfo call, the session or the vault; it never fails a login (a declined/raising refresh keeps the provider's credential, with a warning) and the rotation inherits the login's provider_user_id / id_token / scopes when it omits them. AzureAuth wires both login paths (auth_callback and the username/password branch). (a) TokenResponse gains issued_at — the access token's own iat, read unverified via jwt_issued_at and documented as observability only — plus age_seconds(); build_user_info publishes external_issued_at beside external_expires_at, and get_live_provider_token republishes it after a rotation, so a provider-cached token is visible without decoding anything. (c) New AZURE_LOGIN_PROMPT setting (empty by default, so login UX is unchanged) sends the OIDC prompt on the authorization request; `login` makes Entra re-authenticate and issue instead of replaying its cache — this is the supported lever for point 2 of the revised spec §8 Q1 protocol, and §8 Q1 plus §7 Known Risks, docs/vault.rst, docs/settings.rst, the /api/v1/demo/token-claims instrument and CHANGELOG.md were updated accordingly. Covered by 15 new tests: TestStaleLoginGrant (8) in tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py, TestIssuedAt (5) in tests/unit/identity/test_token_response.py, TestAuthCallbackFreshness (2) in tests/test_azure_token_verifier.py. Full suite: 37 failed / 1589 passed / 4 skipped, FAILED node-id set identical to the recorded FEAT-103 baseline (zero new failures). Independent codex review of the uncommitted diff raised no findings. NOT fixed by this (unchanged by design): the Navigator JWT minted by validate_user_info still carries the pre-refresh external_expires_at in its extra claims, since the login-path refresh happens after the grant is captured but the session — the system of record — is corrected; and nothing forces a fresh issue when AZURE_LOGIN_PROMPT is empty.
title: Entra reuses its cached access token on re-login, so the new session gets a stale provider token

closed_reason: Fixed: ExternalAuth._vault_upstream_token now returns bool (True only after save_linked_identity succeeds) and capture_login_credential sets CAPTURED_LOGIN_GRANT only on that True, so an unbound grant or a failed vault write leaves the AS-resume legacy re-save available. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestCaptureMarker (2 tests) plus the existing suppression control test.
title: Unbound login still sets CAPTURED_LOGIN_GRANT, suppressing AS-resume legacy re-save
Dev DB auth.user_identities has legacy 'uid' column; UserIdentity.filter() fails on it

closed_reason: Fixed: get_live_provider_token now refreshes under a per-(user, external account) asyncio guard (ExternalAuth._refresh_guard) and re-reads the credential inside it, so a concurrent loser returns the winner's rotation instead of spending a retired refresh token. Guard entries are dropped once nobody holds or awaits them. In-process only — documented in the method's Note; the re-read, not the lock, is what keeps a second worker safe. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestConcurrentRefresh (3 tests; the double-refresh test fails with the guard removed).
title: Concurrent get_live_provider_token calls both refresh; rotated refresh token reuse can fail

closed_reason: Login body dedented out of the `if not result:` cache-miss branch in AzureAuth.authenticate(); a silent-token cache hit now runs the same profile fetch / validate / capture / home_redirect path as the username-password grant. Covered by tests/test_azure_userpass_login.py (3 tests; the cache-hit one fails on the pre-fix code).
title: AzureAuth user/password path: acquire_token_silent cache hit skips the entire login body
FEAT-102 nits: untyped __post_init__(data) and implicit string concatenation in TypeError messages

closed_reason: ensure_identity_columns now runs each migration file in its own try/except: a failure is logged with the offending filename, the remaining files still run (each guards its own effect on a catalog lookup, so none depends on a previous success), and the set is re-raised afterwards as one RuntimeError naming every failed file, chained to the first exception. setup_identity_columns still never raises, but now logs that summary instead of only the first error. Regression tests in tests/unit/identity/test_identity_migrations.py: a failing 003 no longer prevents 004/005/006 (all six attempted, error names 003 only), and the all-failing case reports 6 of 6. 179 identity unit tests pass; ruff clean.
title: A failing migration in ensure_identity_columns silently blocks every later one

closed_reason: Fixed: get_for_provider_account (and get_by_provider) now rank rows newest-first via the shared _newest_first helper — refreshed_at, then created_at, tie-broken on identity_id — instead of returning rows[0] in driver order. Covered by 4 tests in tests/unit/identity/test_identity_store.py::TestDuplicateRowOrdering.
title: get_for_provider_account picks rows[0] arbitrarily on duplicates

closed_reason: Fixed: IdentityStore.update_tokens now re-seals id_token (only when the refresh returned one, so an omitting provider does not erase the stored copy) and get_live_provider_token republishes session["id_token"] after a rotation, so the published OIDC token no longer outlives its own exp. Covered by tests/unit/identity/test_identity_store.py::TestUpdateTokens and tests/unit/identity/test_external_token_capture.py::TestRefreshedIdToken (4 tests, including the omit-case guard rails).
title: id_token not refreshed
